headline: Oil Plunges on Iran De-escalation While Precious Metals and Copper Advance
paragraphs: Crude oil suffered a severe selloff, with Brent dropping 6.67 percent to EUR 81.74 and WTI falling 5.37 percent to EUR 76.56, hitting 10-week lows. This sharp correction was driven by President Trump signaling military restraint and stating that new strikes on Iran are highly unlikely despite recent shipping attacks. The resulting drop in energy costs boosted broader market sentiment and helped ease inflationary pressures for businesses.

In contrast, precious metals rallied strongly across the board on a weaker US dollar and risk appetite, led by platinum jumping 2.57 percent to EUR 1,405.42, silver gaining 2.31 percent to EUR 47.21, palladium rising 2.06 percent to EUR 921.98, and gold advancing 1.10 percent to EUR 3,669.92. Copper also pushed higher, gaining 1.95 percent to EUR 5.65 per lb, supported by a supply squeeze and procurement scramble in China ahead of key US inflation data.
The euro traded at 1.1226 against the dollar, helping soften the direct impact of dollar-denominated commodity shifts for Irish importers.
